text:
kai: Heads-up — during the EU marketing spike we're seeing repeated pod evictions in eu-west-1. Burst pool fills, scheduler errors about network attach/timeouts, and some jobs never recover. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

maria: Yep saw a few alerts. LB healthchecks flapped then network plugin timed out mounting CNI. Most of the affected pods were in the burst class.

sam: Quick triage: are these evictions OOM or node unreachable?

kai: Node reporting kubelet: failed killing pod; then pod stuck Terminating. Not OOM. Looks like kubelet <-> cniserver comms got delayed under heavy attach churn.

eva: That smells like too much transient attach/detach when we spin many ephemeral burst instances. Two levers: reduce burst concurrency or increase steady reserve in EU to smooth attach rate.

maria: Reducing burst concurrency helps immediate stability but will shift more load to steady which costs more. Need a short-term mitigation + an autoscaler tuning we can commit.

sam: Short term patch I'm proposing: bump eu-west steady_reserve from 8% to 15% and add a cooldown on burst_grant: 60s -> 180s. Canary this in one AZ. Cheap config snippet below:

```yaml
# autoscaler-config (canary eu-west-1a)
region: eu-west-1
steady_reserve_pct: 0.15
burst_enabled: true
burst_max_pct: 0.20
burst_grant_cooldown_s: 180
preempt_smoothing: true
```

eva: Also add an attach-rate limiter on nodepool provisioning to avoid CNI saturation. Eg: `max_attach_per_minute: 6` for the burst pool.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-042 (eu-west-1 burst evictions). Link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-042 :rotating_light:

maria: We should estimate cost impact if steady reserve stays higher for a week — my back-of-envelope: baseline 1200 GPU-hours/week in EU, promo spike +30% -> ~1560 GPU-hours. Extra reserve increases steady hours by ~80 GPU-hours/week -> ~$1.2k at current list rates.

sam: Good to call out. We'll need approval if we sustain that. Meanwhile throttle new onboarding jobs into EU by adding a token bucket at the ingress-router: `tokens_per_minute: 50` per-account. That will prevent sudden bursts from new tenants.

eva: I'll deploy the canary patch to eu-west-1a now. Canary ID: canary-20260305-17. Will monitor CPU/attach latencies and pod Terminating counts.

kai: Thanks. After canary, if stable, roll to other AZs with a 30% step. Also update runbook under /runbooks/eu-burst-handling.md to reflect the new cooldown and attach limiter steps.

maria: Added a TODO in the runbook and created a brief cost note for finance.

sam: If we see the same pattern in apac or na, we should parameterize the cooldown by observed attach latency rather than a flat value.

eva: Agreed. Follow-up: add metric `attach_latency_p95` and a conditional that reduces burst_max_pct when p95 > 800ms.

kai: Great. If canary looks good in 15-20m, we'll move to staged rollout. Otherwise revert and rollback to previous burst_grant_cooldown_s=60. :thumbsup:
